findings.summary: mutate() calls fn(stateFor(lift)) which reads from the stale outer `sets` closure instead of the updater's `s` parameter, so the clobbering bug is not actually fixed.
findings.mechanism: stateFor is defined as `sets[keyFor(lift.id)] ?? seedFor(lift)`, closing over the render-scope `sets` variable. Inside setSets(s => { const nextSets = fn(stateFor(lift)) ... }), stateFor(lift) still reads the outer `sets`, not `s`. If two taps for the same lift are batched into one React update, the second updater invocation sees the same pre-batch `sets` value as the first, so the second write overwrites the first's change instead of composing — the exact same-batch clobbering the refactor was written to prevent.
